items.title: Rescuers scramble for survivors with 180 dead in Colombia earthquake
items.description: Colombia experienced a number of aftershocks on Tuesday, as efforts continued to free survivors trapped in rubble and buildings.

items.title: Trump says he switched planes after Nato summit because of possible threat
items.description: But the president says the jet he boarded instead was at "greater risk" than the decoy Air Force One.

items.title: Trump's dramatic plane swap hints at personal stakes of Iran war
items.description: It marks another striking episode in the turbulent history of his relationship with Iran, writes the BBC's Anthony Zurcher.

items.title: US says helicopter fired missiles to disable ship breaking Iran blockade
items.description: US Central Command says its helicopter hit the engine room of a Panama-flagged cargo vessel in the Gulf of Oman.

items.title: Baby Shark Boy set to make K-pop debut
items.description: The boy from the most-watched YouTube video of all time is now 17 years old, and wants to be a K-pop star.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo marries long-time partner Georgina Rodríguez
items.description: The Portuguese superstar has posted an image of two hands - presumed to be his on top of his wife's - both wearing wedding rings.

items.title: Lebanon parliament votes to abolish death penalty
items.description: The new law - which next goes to the cabinet for approval - would make Lebanon the first country in the Middle East to end capital punishment.

items.title: Bondi Beach shooting hero's assault charges dropped by police
items.description: Police charged Ahmed al Ahmed in June after an alleged incident with his father at a Sydney home.

items.title: New Zealand PM survives second leadership challenge ahead of election
items.description: Christopher Luxon says he has "full support" of his party, after a vote of confidence 12 weeks before a general election.

items.title: France bans unsolicited telemarketing calls
items.description: Cold calling is coming to an end in France, with one consumer group calling the ban a "small revolution".

items.title: Former judge removed by Orbán elected Hungarian president
items.description: Since taking office in early May, the new Hungarian government has lost no time dismantling Viktor Orbán's legacy.

items.title: Russia using North Korean missiles to strike Ukraine, Zelensky says
items.description: Ukraine's president says strikes in Zaporizhzhia - which killed seven people - involved ballistic missiles from Russia's ally.

items.title: Luigi Mangione murder trial to have anonymous jury
items.description: The judge overseeing the state murder trial ruled the 12-person jury would remain anonymous because of the intense media spotlight on the case.

items.title: Ousted Syrian dictator Bashar al-Assad sentenced to death in absentia
items.description: The ex-president is convicted of committing war crimes and crimes against humanity during the country's civil war.

items.title: Russia releases former US Marine reported in poor health
items.description: Robert Gilman, who was arrested in 2022, was left in "life-threatening condition" after being subjected to "harsh and abusive treatment", his family says.

items.title: Thailand suspends new gun permits after mass shooting
items.description: Authorities promise tough new laws in the country, which has high levels of firearms ownership.

items.title: Canada flight cancelled after child refuses to wear seat belt
items.description: The incident has sparked a debate over child safety and discipline on commercial planes.

items.title: These seaside apartments were a ghost city - then police say scammers moved in
items.description: Malaysia's Forest City was pitched as "paradise" but last month police raided it over alleged scam operations.

items.title: Inside the Secret Service 'shell game' to hide US presidents in plain sight
items.description: Elaborate deception operations and decoys are often used to deceive potential threats to the US president.

items.title: Anguish of Colombian brother at rubble of building being searched for earthquake survivors
items.description: BBC Mundo has gone to the site of Torres del Limonar, a collapsed building in Cali where rescue workers fight to free survivors.
